newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujimori says no need to up security for investors.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori says no need to up security for investors.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said in Japan on Thursday that Lima did not need to take additional security steps to attract foreign investment, despite its four-month hostage crisis.
"We don't need complementary measures," Fujimori told a news conference in Tokyo.

The hostage crisis ended on April 22 when Peruvian commandos stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to free 72 hostages held since December 17 by rebels of the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement.
A Peruvian hostage, two commandos and all 14 Peruvian captors died in the assault.
"(A hostage siege) could happen anywhere in the world, even in Japan. We consider it an isolated issue," said Fujimori, who arrived in Japan on Wednesday for a six-day visit.
"I hope they (Japanese investors) are convinced that there is no need for complementary measures," he said.
In a meeting with Fujimori earlier on Thursday, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto pledged to extend 42.67 billion yen ($374 million) in loans to Peru in the current fiscal year to next March.
Peru, home to some 80,000 people of Japanese ancestry, is the biggest recipient of Japanese economic aid in Latin America. It had received a total of 200 billion yen ($1.75 billion) up until 1995.
Fujimori's visit is his eighth to Japan since he became president in 1990.
Fujimori, the son of Japanese immigrants to Peru, is to make a tour of Japan's main northern island of Hokkaido on Saturday and Sunday to view agricultural techniques. ($1=114 yen)
